questions.question: What does the abbreviation BPE stand for in the context of tokenization?
questions.explanation:
BPE is defined as byte‑pair encoding, a tokenization algorithm introduced in the chapter. (Source Page: [11])  

---

questions.question: Which two tokenization algorithms are identified as being widely used in modern language models?

options.A: Byte‑pair encoding (BPE) and unigram language modeling
options.D: Regular expression tokenization and minimum edit distance

questions.explanation:
The text explicitly states that BPE and unigram language modeling are the two widely used tokenization algorithms. (Source Page: [10])  

---

questions.question: Why is standardizing tokenization considered essential for NLP experiments?

options.A: It improves the speed of model training.
options.B: It ensures replicability and allows metrics like perplexity to be applied correctly.
options.C: It reduces the size of the vocabulary needed.
options.D: It enables the use of Unicode code points.

questions.explanation:
Standardization is necessary for replicability, and many algorithms (e.g., perplexity) assume a fixed tokenization. (Source Page: [10])  

---

questions.question: Alongside Unicode code points, which encoding format is introduced in the chapter?
questions.explanation:
The chapter discusses Unicode code points together with the UTF‑8 encoding. (Source Page: [32])

questions.question: Which algorithm is mentioned as a method for comparing strings?
questions.explanation:
The minimum edit distance algorithm is listed among the tools introduced for string comparison. (Source Page: [32])  

---

questions.question: What linguistic levels are covered when discussing tokens and tokenization?
questions.explanation:
The chapter outlines tokens at the levels of words, morphemes, and characters. (Source Page: [32])

questions.question: In the BPE algorithm, what is the primary operation performed repeatedly during token construction?

options.B: Merging the most frequent pair of adjacent symbols
options.D: Replacing tokens with their Unicode code points

questions.explanation:
BPE works by iteratively merging the most frequent adjacent byte (or symbol) pairs to build larger tokens. (Source Page: [11][32])  

---

questions.question: Which evaluation metric mentioned in the text assumes that all texts have a fixed tokenization?
questions.explanation:
The perplexity metric for language models assumes a fixed tokenization of the input texts. (Source Page: [10])  

---

questions.question: The BPE algorithm for tokenization was popularized in which publication year?
questions.explanation:
The BPE method for machine translation was introduced by Sennrich et al. in 2016. (Source Page: [11])

questions.question: What purpose does the regular expression tool serve in the context of this chapter?

options.A: To encode Unicode characters into UTF‑8
options.B: To define patterns for tokenizing text
options.C: To compute the minimum edit distance between strings

questions.explanation: Regular expressions are introduced as a means to specify patterns used in tokenization. (Source Page: [32])
